# Model and source

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Tsai_2024_vancomycin")()$reference`
* Description: `r readModelDb("Tsai_2024_vancomycin")()$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40121-024-01071-5> (open access)
* Supplement (Tables S1-S4, Figure S1): Electronic Supplementary Material 1 at
  the article landing page.

Tsai and colleagues sampled vancomycin densely in critically ill adults in a
cardiac intensive care unit, about half of whom were on temporary mechanical
circulatory support (tMCS: VA-ECMO, VV-ECMO or an extracorporeal CentriMag
ventricular assist device) and a quarter on continuous renal replacement
therapy (CRRT). Both supports were recorded as **time-varying** states, because
patients were frequently decannulated or taken off CRRT during a vancomycin
course.

The final model is a two-compartment model with three features worth noting:

1. **Two clearance arms.** Off CRRT, clearance falls with serum creatinine
   (`CL = 2.85 * Cr^-0.69 * (WT/70)^0.73` L/h, creatinine in mg/dL and
   uncentred). On CRRT the creatinine term is dropped and a separate typical
   value is used (`CL = 2.30 * (WT/70)^0.73` L/h). Both arms share one
   between-subject random effect (Supplementary Table S1, Model 3).
2. **CRRT expands the central volume** by `exp(0.54)` = 1.72-fold.
3. **tMCS lowers intercompartmental clearance** by `exp(-0.66)` = 0.52-fold and
   changes nothing else. Because AUC depends only on CL, tMCS leaves the daily
   AUC unchanged while it lowers the trough and raises the peak. The authors'
   point is that trough-guided dosing therefore misleads under tMCS.

# Population

Twenty-five adults (24 men, 96%) contributed 184 plasma samples at a single
centre in Tainan, Taiwan, between January 2018 and March 2022 (Tsai 2024
Table 1). Median age was 61 years (IQR 49-66), median weight 68.8 kg (IQR
61.0-82.1), median APACHE II score 24 and median serum creatinine 1.1 mg/dL
(IQR 0.8-1.7). At the index (sampled) dose 14 patients were on tMCS (11 VA-ECMO,
1 VV-ECMO, 1 BiVAD, 1 LVAD) and 6 on CRRT (4 CVVH, 2 CVVHDF; median effluent
flow 29.7 mL/kg/h); no patient received intermittent haemodialysis. The index
dose was a median 900 mg infused over 1.8 h after a median of six earlier
doses, and was sampled pre-dose and 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 and 12 h after the end
of infusion.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Tsai_2024_vancomycin")()$population`.

```{r population}
pop <- readModelDb("Tsai_2024_vancomycin")()$population
str(pop[c("species", "n_subjects", "n_observations", "age_range", "weight_range")])
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` entry carries an in-file comment naming its source location. The
table below collects them for review.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lvc` (Vc off CRRT) | log(13.49 L) | Table 2, theta1 |
| `e_crrt_vc` (CRRT on Vc) | 0.54 | Table 2, theta2; `Vc = theta1 x exp(theta2) if CRRT` |
| `lcl` (CL off CRRT at Cr = 1 mg/dL, 70 kg) | log(2.85 L/h) | Table 2, theta3 |
| `lcl_crrt` (CL on CRRT at 70 kg) | log(2.30 L/h) | Table 2, theta4 |
| `e_creat_cl` (Cr exponent, off CRRT only) | -0.69 | Table 2, theta5; Supplementary Table S1 Model 3 |
| `e_wt_cl` (weight exponent, both arms) | 0.73 | Table 2, theta6 |
| `lvp` | log(32.68 L) | Table 2, theta7 |
| `lq` (Q without tMCS) | log(18.81 L/h) | Table 2, theta8 |
| `e_mcs_temp_q` (tMCS on Q) | -0.66 | Table 2, theta9; `Q = theta8 x exp(theta9) if tMCS` |
| `etalcl` | 0.100 (variance) | Table 2, omega CL (IIV 32.4%) |
| `etalvp` | 0.095 (variance) | Table 2, omega Vp (IIV 31.7%) |
| `etalq` | 0.081 (variance) | Table 2, omega Q (IIV 29.1%) |
| no eta on Vc | -- | Table 2 ('-'); Results: removed for high shrinkage |
| `addSd` | 1.39 mg/L | Table 2, residual variability (additive) |
| Two-compartment structure, IV infusion | -- | Results, 'Population PK Model'; Table 2 |
| Shared eta on both CL arms | -- | Supplementary Table S1, Model 3 (11 parameters, -2LL 850.5) |

The Table 2 footnote defines `IIV% = sqrt(exp(omega) - 1)` with omega the
variance. The printed IIV percentages reproduce from the printed omegas to
within the rounding of the three-decimal omegas (32.4 / 31.6 / 29.0 versus the
printed 32.4 / 31.7 / 29.1%), which confirms they are exponential-model
variances. Read as standard deviations, the same numbers would give an IIV of
about 10%.

```{r omega-check}
omega <- c(CL = 0.100, Vp = 0.095, Q = 0.081)
iiv_pct <- 100 * sqrt(exp(omega) - 1)
round(iiv_pct, 2)
# Rounding omega to 3 decimals moves IIV% by up to ~0.08 points.
stopifnot(all(abs(iiv_pct - c(32.4, 31.7, 29.1)) < 0.15))
```

# Per-kilogram values printed in the Discussion

The Discussion restates the typical values per kilogram of the median cohort
weight (68.8 kg). These are deterministic functions of the model and are
checked exactly against the printed rounding.

```{r discussion-check}
mod <- readModelDb("Tsai_2024_vancomycin")
ini_tab <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$iniDf
th <- setNames(ini_tab$est, ini_tab$name)
wt <- 68.8
per_kg <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quantity, ~model, ~printed, ~digits,
  "Vc off CRRT (L/kg)", exp(th[["lvc"]]) / wt, 0.20, 2,
  "Vc on CRRT (L/kg), 0.2 * exp(theta2)", 0.2 * exp(th[["e_crrt_vc"]]), 0.34, 2,
  "Vp (L/kg)", exp(th[["lvp"]]) / wt, 0.48, 2,
  "CL off CRRT, Cr 1 mg/dL (L/h/kg)", exp(th[["lcl"]]) * (wt / 70)^th[["e_wt_cl"]] / wt, 0.041, 3,
  "Q ratio under tMCS", exp(th[["e_mcs_temp_q"]]), 0.52, 2
)
per_kg$rounded <- mapply(round, per_kg$model, per_kg$digits)
per_kg |>
  dplyr::select(-digits) |>
  dplyr::rename("Quantity" = quantity, "Model" = model, "Printed" = printed, "Model, rounded" = rounded) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, caption = "Discussion per-kg values reproduced from the packaged model.")
stopifnot(all(per_kg$rounded == per_kg$printed))
```

# Typical-value regimen: Figure 6 and the 70 kg, Cr 1 mg/dL row of Table 4

Figure 6 fully specifies one regimen: 70 kg, serum creatinine 1 mg/dL, a
20 mg/kg loading dose and 20 mg/kg/day maintenance given every 12 h. Infusions
last 2 h (Methods, Simulation). The maintenance doses are taken to start one
dosing interval after the load. The figure switches tMCS status at 120 h in
both directions.

```{r helpers}
# One subject's event table: a loading dose, then maintenance every `tau` h
# from `tau` to `t_end`, 2-h infusions, and a dense observation grid on the
# central compartment. `mcs_switch` (h) flips MCS_TEMP_STATUS from `mcs` to
# 1 - mcs at that time.
make_regimen <- function(id, wt, creat, crrt, mcs, ld_mgkg, md_mgkg_day,
                         tau = 12, t_end = 240, mcs_switch = Inf, dt = 0.25) {
  dose_t <- c(0, seq(tau, t_end - tau, by = tau))
  dose_amt <- c(ld_mgkg * wt, rep(md_mgkg_day * wt * tau / 24, length(dose_t) - 1))
  keep <- dose_amt > 0
  doses <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = dose_t[keep], amt = dose_amt[keep], rate = dose_amt[keep] / 2,
    evid = 1L, cmt = "central"
  )
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = seq(0, t_end, by = dt), amt = 0, rate = 0,
    evid = 0L, cmt = "central"
  )
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |> dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  ev$WT <- wt
  ev$CREAT <- creat
  ev$RRT_CRRT_ACTIVE <- crrt
  ev$MCS_TEMP_STATUS <- ifelse(ev$time < mcs_switch, mcs, 1 - mcs)
  ev
}
mod_tv <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
solve_tv <- function(ev) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_tv, events = ev, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6))
}
```

```{r figure-6}
fig6_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_regimen(1L, 70, 1, 0, mcs = 0, 20, 20, mcs_switch = 120) |>
    dplyr::mutate(panel = "non-tMCS to tMCS"),
  make_regimen(2L, 70, 1, 0, mcs = 1, 20, 20, mcs_switch = 120) |>
    dplyr::mutate(panel = "tMCS to non-tMCS")
)
fig6 <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_tv,
  events = fig6_ev, keep = c("panel", "MCS_TEMP_STATUS"),
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
))
ggplot(fig6, aes(time, Cc, colour = factor(MCS_TEMP_STATUS), group = 1)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(15, 20), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("0" = "#d7301f", "1" = "#1f9eb4"), name = "tMCS") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 240, 48)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Vancomycin Cc (mg/L)",
    title = "70 kg, Cr 1 mg/dL, 20 mg/kg load + 20 mg/kg/day q12h",
    caption = "Typical-value replication of Figure 6 of Tsai 2024."
  )
```

```{r figure-6-auc}
# Rolling 24-h AUC of the typical subject on each side of the switch: the
# tMCS status changes Q only, so the daily AUC must not move.
auc24 <- function(sim, from) {
  s <- sim[sim$time >= from & sim$time <= from + 24, ]
  sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$Cc, -1) + tail(s$Cc, -1)) / 2)
}
fig6_auc <- fig6 |>
  dplyr::group_by(panel) |>
  dplyr::group_modify(~ data.frame(
    window = c("96-120 h", "192-216 h"),
    auc24 = c(auc24(.x, 96), auc24(.x, 192))
  )) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
knitr::kable(fig6_auc, digits = 1, caption = "Typical-value 24-h AUC (mg*h/L) before and after the tMCS switch.")
# Daily dose / CL = 1400 / 2.85 = 491 mg*h/L once near steady state; the
# switch must leave it unchanged. The 0.5% bound is far above the trapezoid
# error at a 0.25-h grid and far below the 48% change in Q.
stopifnot(
  nrow(fig6_auc) == 4L,
  all(abs(fig6_auc$auc24 / (1400 / 2.85) - 1) < 0.02),
  abs(fig6_auc$auc24[1] / fig6_auc$auc24[2] - 1) < 0.005,
  abs(fig6_auc$auc24[3] / fig6_auc$auc24[4] - 1) < 0.005
)
```

The typical-value curves reproduce the shape of Figure 6: the tMCS segment has
higher peaks and lower troughs at the same daily AUC (about 490 mg\*h/L, the
orange dashed line of the figure). The figure caption calls the tMCS line red
and the non-tMCS line green, but the figure's own legend (`tMCS 0` red, `1`
teal) and panel titles show the reverse; the colours above follow the legend.

Table 4 reports the population **mean** trough at 48 h for this regimen as
14.2 mg/L without and 13.4 mg/L with tMCS (also quoted in the Abstract, which
prints the unit as mg/dL). The typical-value trough sits slightly below the
population mean, as expected for a log-normally distributed clearance.

```{r table-4-70kg}
trough_tv <- function(wt, creat, crrt, mcs, ld, md, tau = 12) {
  s <- solve_tv(make_regimen(1L, wt, creat, crrt, mcs, ld, md, tau = tau, t_end = 60))
  s$Cc[s$time == 48]
}
row70 <- tibble::tibble(
  arm = c("non-tMCS", "tMCS"),
  paper_mean = c(14.2, 13.4),
  model_typical = c(trough_tv(70, 1, 0, 0, 20, 20), trough_tv(70, 1, 0, 1, 20, 20))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model_typical / paper_mean - 1))
row70 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm, "Table 4 mean trough (mg/L)" = paper_mean,
    "Typical-value trough (mg/L)" = model_typical, "% diff" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "48-h trough, 70 kg, Cr 1 mg/dL, 20 mg/kg load + 20 mg/kg/day q12h.")
# Measured -1.8% / -1.9%. A mis-transcribed CL, Vc, Q or tMCS effect moves
# the trough by tens of percent; 5% leaves room for the mean-vs-typical gap.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(row70$pct_diff) < 5),
  # The tMCS-induced drop: paper 0.8 mg/L.
  abs(diff(rev(row70$model_typical)) - 0.8) < 0.15
)
```

# Table 4: all scenarios

Table 4 lists the regimen with the best average probability of target
attainment over the first 48 h for 15 scenarios (60, 70 and 80 kg crossed with
creatinine 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 mg/dL or CRRT), with the mean 48-h trough under each
tMCS status. The table does not state the dosing interval of each regimen
(Figure 4 explores every 6, 8 or 12 h), so the absolute troughs below assume
every 12 h and are shown for orientation only. The **ratio** of the tMCS to the
non-tMCS trough is a property of the Q effect and is compared directly.

```{r table-4}
t4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~wt, ~renal, ~ld, ~md, ~trough_tmcs, ~trough_non,
  60, "Cr=0.5", 25, 30, 13.4, 14.5,
  60, "Cr=1", 25, 20, 13.9, 14.7,
  60, "Cr=2", 15, 15, 17.6, 18.4,
  60, "Cr=4", 15, 10, 17.8, 18.4,
  60, "CRRT", 25, 15, 17.8, 17.6,
  70, "Cr=0.5", 25, 30, 10.8, 11.5,
  70, "Cr=1", 20, 20, 13.4, 14.2,
  70, "Cr=2", 15, 15, 17.1, 18.0,
  70, "Cr=4", 15, 10, 17.7, 18.3,
  70, "CRRT", 20, 15, 16.9, 17.5,
  80, "Cr=0.5", 20, 30, 12.1, 13.3,
  80, "Cr=1", 20, 20, 12.7, 13.5,
  80, "Cr=2", 15, 10, 15.3, 15.8,
  80, "Cr=4", 15, 10, 17.3, 18.0,
  80, "CRRT", 20, 15, 16.5, 17.1
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    crrt = as.integer(renal == "CRRT"),
    # CREAT does not enter the CRRT arm; any positive value is inert there.
    creat = ifelse(crrt == 1L, 1, suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("Cr=", "", renal))))
  )
stopifnot(nrow(t4) == 15L, !anyNA(t4$creat))
t4$model_tmcs <- mapply(trough_tv, t4$wt, t4$creat, t4$crrt, 1L, t4$ld, t4$md)
t4$model_non <- mapply(trough_tv, t4$wt, t4$creat, t4$crrt, 0L, t4$ld, t4$md)
t4 <- t4 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ratio_paper = trough_tmcs / trough_non,
    ratio_model = model_tmcs / model_non
  )
t4 |>
  dplyr::select(wt, renal, ld, md, trough_non, model_non, trough_tmcs, model_tmcs, ratio_paper, ratio_model) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "BW (kg)" = wt, "Renal" = renal, "Load (mg/kg)" = ld, "Maint. (mg/kg/day)" = md,
    "Paper non-tMCS" = trough_non, "Model non-tMCS (q12h)" = model_non,
    "Paper tMCS" = trough_tmcs, "Model tMCS (q12h)" = model_tmcs,
    "Paper ratio" = ratio_paper, "Model ratio" = ratio_model
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "48-h trough (mg/L): Table 4 population means versus typical-value model troughs.")
```

```{r table-4-gate}
ratio_diff <- t4$ratio_model - t4$ratio_paper
summary(ratio_diff)
# The model ratio is 0.93-0.97 in every scenario. The paper's ratios,
# formed from means rounded to 0.1 mg/L, scatter around it (0.91-1.01); the
# 60 kg CRRT row, where the paper's tMCS mean is ABOVE the non-tMCS mean, is
# the outlier. Gate the centre, not the extremes.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(ratio_diff)) < 0.02,
  all(t4$ratio_model < 1)
)
```

The tMCS effect on the trough is reproduced across the table: the model lowers
the 48-h trough by 3-7% under tMCS in every scenario, and the paper's ratios
centre on the same value. The absolute troughs agree closely where the q12h
assumption is likely (creatinine 1 mg/dL), and fall below the paper's means in
scenarios whose optimal regimen probably used a shorter interval (creatinine
0.5 mg/dL, CRRT); this is a limitation of the transcribed table, not of the
model.

# Stochastic replication of the 70 kg, Cr 1 mg/dL scenario

Table 4 also reports, for the Figure 6 regimen, the mean +/- SD 48-h trough
and the probability that the 24-h AUC lands in 400-600 mg\*h/L averaged over
the first 48 h. Two hundred virtual 70 kg patients per arm are simulated with
between-subject variability and residual error.

```{r stochastic}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241112)
n_per_arm <- 200L
stoch_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(0:1, function(m) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_per_arm), function(i) {
    make_regimen(m * n_per_arm + i, 70, 1, 0, mcs = m, 20, 20, t_end = 48, dt = 0.5)
  })) |>
    dplyr::mutate(arm = ifelse(m == 1L, "tMCS", "non-tMCS"))
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(stoch_ev[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
stoch <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = stoch_ev, keep = "arm", maxsteps = 1e6))

trough48 <- stoch |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 48) |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_trough = mean(sim), sd_trough = sd(sim), .groups = "drop")

pta <- stoch |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    auc_0_24 = sum(diff(time[time <= 24]) * (head(ipredSim[time <= 24], -1) + tail(ipredSim[time <= 24], -1)) / 2),
    auc_24_48 = sum(diff(time[time >= 24]) * (head(ipredSim[time >= 24], -1) + tail(ipredSim[time >= 24], -1)) / 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    pta_400_600 = 100 * mean(c(auc_0_24 >= 400 & auc_0_24 <= 600, auc_24_48 >= 400 & auc_24_48 <= 600)),
    pta_400 = 100 * mean(c(auc_0_24 >= 400, auc_24_48 >= 400)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stoch_tab <- dplyr::left_join(trough48, pta, by = "arm") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    paper_mean = c(14.2, 13.4)[match(arm, c("non-tMCS", "tMCS"))],
    paper_sd = c(3.0, 2.8)[match(arm, c("non-tMCS", "tMCS"))],
    paper_pta = c(62.2, 61.8)[match(arm, c("non-tMCS", "tMCS"))],
    paper_pta400 = c(78.9, 78.7)[match(arm, c("non-tMCS", "tMCS"))]
  )
stoch_tab |>
  dplyr::select(arm, paper_mean, mean_trough, paper_sd, sd_trough, paper_pta, pta_400_600, paper_pta400, pta_400) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm,
    "Trough mean, paper" = paper_mean, "Trough mean, model" = mean_trough,
    "Trough SD, paper" = paper_sd, "Trough SD, model" = sd_trough,
    "PTA 400-600 %, paper" = paper_pta, "PTA 400-600 %, model" = pta_400_600,
    "AUC >= 400 %, paper" = paper_pta400, "AUC >= 400 %, model" = pta_400
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "70 kg, Cr 1 mg/dL, 20 mg/kg load + 20 mg/kg/day q12h: 200 virtual patients per arm.")

# Mean trough: SD of the mean ~0.4 mg/L at n = 200 (~3%); 12% is several
# standard errors away from the measured ~1-4% gap and still fails on a
# structural transcription error.
stopifnot(
  nrow(stoch_tab) == 2L,
  all(abs(stoch_tab$mean_trough / stoch_tab$paper_mean - 1) < 0.12)
)
```

```{r vpc-plot}
stoch |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = quantile(sim, 0.5), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Vancomycin Cc (mg/L)",
    title = "Median and 90% prediction interval, first 48 h",
    caption = "200 virtual 70 kg patients per arm, Cr 1 mg/dL, 20 mg/kg load + 20 mg/kg/day q12h."
  )
```

The mean trough and the AUC-based target attainment agree with Table 4, and
the model reproduces the paper's finding that the AUC-based PTA is unchanged
by tMCS while the trough falls. The model's trough SD is wider than the
roughly 3 mg/L printed in Table 4. With a 32% CV on clearance and an additive
1.39 mg/L residual, a between-patient SD near 3 mg/L at a 14 mg/L mean is not
attainable, so the printed SD may describe a different spread than the
between-patient one (for example, without between-subject variability); the
paper does not say.

# PKNCA: index-dose NCA against Supplementary Table S2

Supplementary Table S2 gives the observed non-compartmental analysis of the
sampled index dose stratified by tMCS. The virtual cohort below mirrors the
index-dose design: 900 mg infused over 1.8 h every 12 h, the seventh dose
sampled pre-dose and at 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 and 12 h after the end of infusion,
with no further dose inside that window. Weight and creatinine are drawn log-normally around the Table 1 medians, and
the CRRT fraction per arm follows Table S2. The observed medians come from only
11 and 14 patients with heterogeneous dosing histories, so the comparison is
approximate.

```{r nca-cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2617)
set.seed(2617)
make_index_arm <- function(n, mcs, frac_crrt, id_offset) {
  subj <- tibble::tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    WT = exp(rnorm(n, log(68.8), 0.2)),
    CREAT = exp(rnorm(n, log(1.1), 0.5)),
    RRT_CRRT_ACTIVE = rbinom(n, 1, frac_crrt),
    MCS_TEMP_STATUS = mcs,
    arm = ifelse(mcs == 1L, "tMCS", "non-tMCS")
  )
  dose_t <- seq(0, 72, by = 12)
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(subj, time = dose_t) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 900, rate = 900 / 1.8, evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
  obs_t <- c(72, 72 + 1.8 + c(0.5, 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 12))
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(subj, time = obs_t) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |> dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
idx_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_index_arm(200L, 1L, 2 / 11, 0L),
  make_index_arm(200L, 0L, 5 / 14, 200L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(idx_ev[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
idx_sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = idx_ev, keep = "arm", maxsteps = 1e6))
```

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- idx_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, arm)
dose_df <- idx_ev |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, arm)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id)
# CL_obs and Vd_obs are taken as dose / AUC0-inf and CL / lambda-z of the
# index dose, extrapolated from concentrations that still carry the earlier
# doses -- the naive single-dose NCA that a sampled index dose yields.
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 72, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE, vz.obs = TRUE,
  half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm, ~cmax, ~cl.obs, ~vz.obs, ~half.life,
  "tMCS", 26.5, 1.6, 35.6, 12.6,
  "non-tMCS", 41.6, 1.3, 24.2, 11.6
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "arm",
  params = c("cmax", "half.life", "cl.obs", "vz.obs"),
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", cl.obs = "L/h", vz.obs = "L", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
# The comparison is IV: relabel PKNCA's generic CL/F and Vz/F.
cmp[[1]] <- sub("CL/F", "CL_obs = dose / AUC0-inf", cmp[[1]], fixed = TRUE)
cmp[[1]] <- sub("Vz/F", "Vd_obs = CL_obs / lambda-z", cmp[[1]], fixed = TRUE)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Index-dose NCA: median of the virtual cohort versus the observed medians of Supplementary Table S2. * differs by >20%."
)
```

The supplement does not define CL_obs and Vd_obs. Read as the naive
single-dose NCA of the sampled dose (dose over an AUC0-inf that is extrapolated
from concentrations still carrying the earlier doses, and Vd_obs as CL_obs
over the terminal slope), the non-tMCS arm is reproduced closely: clearance, volume and
peak all fall within 10% of the observed medians. Read instead as dose over the
12-h AUC, simulated clearance would be about twice the observed value, so this
reading is the one the data support. The simulated half-life runs about 25%
above both observed medians, whose interquartile ranges (8.4-44.7 h and
10.8-16.2 h) are wide.

The tMCS arm is not reproduced: the observed tMCS peak (26.5 mg/L) is lower
than the non-tMCS one and the observed volume larger. The final model cannot
produce that pattern for any patient. tMCS lowers Q only, which raises the
post-infusion peak and leaves the volumes unchanged. The authors' covariate
search tested the presence, mode and flow of tMCS and retained only its effect
on Q (Methods; Supplementary Table S3), so the observed tMCS medians reflect
differences between these 11 patients that the final model does not attribute
to tMCS. Two further cautions apply:

* The observed medians come from 11 and 14 patients whose earlier doses,
  amounts and creatinine trajectories varied, while the virtual cohort uses one
  fixed 900 mg q12h history.
* Table S2's group sizes (11 tMCS, 14 non-tMCS) are the reverse of Table 1's
  index-dose counts (14 on tMCS, 11 without), and its CRRT total (7) matches
  Table 1's first-dose count rather than its index-dose count (6). The values
  are used as printed.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Residual error scale.** Table 2 prints the additive residual as 1.39 without
  stating whether it is a standard deviation or a variance. The model was fit
  in Phoenix NLME 8.2, whose residual-error estimate is a standard deviation,
  so `addSd = 1.39` mg/L is used. Read as a variance it would be 1.18 mg/L.
- **Which clearance arm carries creatinine.** The Results prose says "an
  independent CL for non-CRRT with BW as a covariate and an independent CL for
  CRRT with serum Cr and BW as covariates", which puts creatinine on the CRRT
  arm. The printed equation in Table 2, Supplementary Table S1 (Model 3:
  "Cr as a covariate only on CL for non-dialysis") and the Discussion
  ("Cr level on decreasing the CL for non-CRRT") all put it on the non-CRRT
  arm, and that reading is used.
- **Creatinine is uncentred.** `CL = theta3 * Cr^theta5 * (BW/70)^theta6`
  takes creatinine in mg/dL with no reference value, so `theta3` is the
  clearance at 1 mg/dL. `CREAT` must be a positive number on every record,
  including CRRT records where it has no effect.
- **tMCS covariate.** The paper's tMCS pools VA-ECMO, VV-ECMO and
  extracorporeal VAD (2 of the 14 supported patients were on a CentriMag VAD,
  not ECMO), so it does not map onto `ECMO_STATUS`. The maintainers registered
  the broader canonical `MCS_TEMP_STATUS` for it.
- **CRRT covariate.** CRRT changed within the vancomycin course for one
  patient, so it is encoded with the time-varying gate `RRT_CRRT_ACTIVE`.
- **Table 4 dosing interval.** Table 4 does not give the interval of its
  recommended regimens; the troughs above assume every 12 h, which Figure 6
  states for the 70 kg, Cr 1 mg/dL regimen. Maintenance doses are assumed to
  start one interval after the loading dose.
- **Table 4 trough SD.** The model's between-patient spread of the 48-h trough
  is wider than the roughly 3 mg/L SD printed in Table 4; see the stochastic
  section above.
- **Figure 6 colours.** The caption labels the colours the opposite way from
  the figure's legend and panel titles; the legend is followed.
- **No erratum** to Tsai 2024 was found as of 2026-10-15.
